name: dev.heyidentity/heyidentity
title: HeyIdentity
description: Create a fake Entra ID or OIDC tenant for testing in one call. No account needed.

tools.name: remove_custom_claim
tools.description: Removes a custom claim.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

name.description: The name of the claim to remove.

tools.name: create_configuration
tools.description: Creates another configuration in the tenant from the starter content (a demo user and a demo client), with a name unique in the tenant and a profile. Prefer a separate client per environment in one configuration; create a configuration for a different profile or a separate set of users. A retry with the same name answers configuration_exists with the existing configuration instead of creating a second one.

name.description: The configuration's name, at most 200 characters and unique in the tenant ignoring case, e.g. staging.

profile.description: Optional profile: Generic (default), Microsoft (Entra ID), or AzureAdB2C (one synthetic sign-in policy).

tools.name: remove_user
tools.description: Removes a user (at least one must remain).

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

key.description: The key of the user to remove.

tools.name: edit_settings
tools.description: Edits the settings; fields left out keep their value. settings: { profile?, b2c_policy_claim? (tfp or acr), validate_client_secrets?, token_lifetime_minutes?, token_shape?: { scope_claim_name?, scope_claim_format?, roles_claim_name?, roles_nested_key?, access_token_audience? } }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

b2c_policy_claim.description: AzureAdB2C policy claim: tfp (default) or acr (legacy). An omitted field preserves the stored setting, including across profile switches.

validate_client_secrets.description: Require client secrets at the token endpoint.

roles_claim_name.description: Where roles are emitted, e.g. realm_access; roles when not set.

roles_nested_key.description: Nests roles under this key of roles_claim_name, e.g. roles for realm_access.roles.

access_token_audience.description: Whether the audience is sent as aud (default) or as client_id with no aud (like Cognito); Generic profile only, see the audience rule.

token_shape.description: Claim shape options (Generic profile only); fields left out keep their value.

settings.description: The settings to change. The configuration's settings. Fields left out keep their value.

tools.name: get_configuration
tools.description: Returns one configuration of the tenant as items: clients, users, custom and standard claims, settings and endpoints.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

tools.name: request_claim_code
tools.description: Issues a single-use claim code for an unclaimed tenant. It works for 15 minutes and replaces any earlier code. Show the code and claim_page_url to the user; never store the code.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Describes the profiles (claims, URL shapes, protocol behaviors), token shape options, standard claims, limits, the current terms version and the rules agents must follow. Read it before configuring a tenant.

tools.name: remove_client
tools.description: Removes a client.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

client_id.description: The id of the client to remove.

tools.name: create_tenant
tools.description: Creates an unverified HeyIdentity test tenant with a working demo client and test user, accepting the current Terms of Use on behalf of the operator running the agent. Returns endpoints, an agent token, the fixed claim page URL, the expiry time and next_steps.

accepted_terms_version.description: The current Terms of Use version (see get_catalog), accepted on behalf of the operator running the agent.

display_name.description: Optional display name of the tenant.

profile.description: Optional profile: Generic (default), Microsoft (Entra ID), or AzureAdB2C (one synthetic sign-in policy).

idempotency_key.description: Strongly recommended: a random secret of 32 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ (for example crypto.randomUUID()), generated once per intended tenant and kept secret like the agent token. Retrying with the same value and arguments, only if you never received the response, returns the same tenant instead of creating another.

tools.name: edit_user
tools.description: Edits a user; fields left out keep their value, and claims, when given, replace the user's claims.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

key.description: The key of the user to edit.
The user key shown on the sign-in page and used as sub by default. Required when adding; fixed afterwards.

display_name.description: The name shown on the sign-in page and emitted as the name claim.

sub.description: The sub claim; the key when not set.

icon.description: A built-in icon id for the sign-in page.

access_token_sub.description: A different sub for access tokens only.

claims.description: The user's claims: name to a string, number, boolean or array of strings, e.g. { "email": "alice@example.com", "roles": ["admin"] }. Use fictional people only.

claim_targets.description: Which token each claim goes into: name to both (default), id_token or access_token.

sign_in_outcome.description: How sign-in goes for this user: normal (default), access_denied, temporarily_unavailable, interaction_required (prompt=none fails) or refresh_revoked (refreshing fails with invalid_grant). Any value other than normal is a Pro feature (plan_required otherwise).

changes.description: The fields to change. A fictional test user. On edit, fields left out keep their value; claims, when given, replaces the user's claims.

tools.name: add_client
tools.description: Adds a client. client: { client_id, client_secret?, allow_all_return_urls?, redirect_uris?, allowed_scopes?, exposed_scopes?, access_token_audience? }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

client_id.description: The client id. Required when adding; fixed afterwards (it is the id in the URL when editing).

client_secret.description: The client secret; checked only when the configuration's validate_client_secrets setting is on.

allow_all_return_urls.description: Accept any redirect URI. Convenient for local tests; default false.

redirect_uris.description: Exact redirect URIs the app uses, e.g. http://localhost:5173/callback (http(s) with a host, or an app scheme such as com.example.app:/callback or myapp://callback).

allowed_scopes.description: Scopes the client may request, e.g. openid, profile, email, offline_access, api://orders/read. Default when adding: openid, profile.

exposed_scopes.description: Scopes this client exposes as an API (resource), e.g. https://weather.example/mcp/tools.read: advertised in discovery scopes_supported. On a Generic configuration each scope's resource (everything before the last /) is an accepted resource parameter value (RFC 8707), which then becomes aud (see the audience rule).

access_token_audience.description: Audience value used when the requesting client's request has no resource and no resource-qualified scope; the client id when not set. On a Generic configuration an absolute URI here, e.g. https://weather.example/mcp, is also an accepted resource parameter value (RFC 8707), which then becomes aud (see the audience rule).

client.description: The client, as in the Agent API. A client (an app that signs in, or an API). On edit, fields left out keep their value.

tools.name: edit_client
tools.description: Edits a client; fields left out keep their value. changes: { client_secret?, allow_all_return_urls?, redirect_uris?, allowed_scopes?, exposed_scopes?, access_token_audience? }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

client_id.description: The id of the client to edit.
The client id. Required when adding; fixed afterwards (it is the id in the URL when editing).

client_secret.description: The client secret; checked only when the configuration's validate_client_secrets setting is on.

allow_all_return_urls.description: Accept any redirect URI. Convenient for local tests; default false.

redirect_uris.description: Exact redirect URIs the app uses, e.g. http://localhost:5173/callback (http(s) with a host, or an app scheme such as com.example.app:/callback or myapp://callback).

allowed_scopes.description: Scopes the client may request, e.g. openid, profile, email, offline_access, api://orders/read. Default when adding: openid, profile.

exposed_scopes.description: Scopes this client exposes as an API (resource), e.g. https://weather.example/mcp/tools.read: advertised in discovery scopes_supported. On a Generic configuration each scope's resource (everything before the last /) is an accepted resource parameter value (RFC 8707), which then becomes aud (see the audience rule).

access_token_audience.description: Audience value used when the requesting client's request has no resource and no resource-qualified scope; the client id when not set. On a Generic configuration an absolute URI here, e.g. https://weather.example/mcp, is also an accepted resource parameter value (RFC 8707), which then becomes aud (see the audience rule).

changes.description: The fields to change. A client (an app that signs in, or an API). On edit, fields left out keep their value.

tools.name: validate_configuration
tools.description: Reports problems (e.g. a client without a redirect URI) and warnings (e.g. a scope no client requests) without changing anything.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

tools.name: add_custom_claim
tools.description: Adds a custom claim emitted for every user. claim: { name, value, target?: both|id_token|access_token }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

name.description: The claim name. Required when adding; fixed afterwards.

claim.description: The custom claim. A custom claim emitted for every user.

tools.name: edit_custom_claim
tools.description: Edits a custom claim's value or target; fields left out keep their value. changes: { value?, target? }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

name.description: The name of the claim to edit.
The claim name. Required when adding; fixed afterwards.

changes.description: The fields to change. A custom claim emitted for every user.

tools.name: set_standard_claims
tools.description: Sets which of the profile's generated standard claims are enabled (see get_configuration's standard_claims.available).

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

enabled.description: The standard claims to enable, e.g. ["auth_time", "jti"]. Required. PUT .../claims/standard replaces the whole list: send the current list (GET /agent/v1/configurations/{configuration_id}) plus the new claim.

tools.name: get_tenant
tools.description: Returns the tenant, its configurations and their endpoints, its limits and status.

tools.name: rotate_signing_key
tools.description: Generates a new RSA signing key for this configuration. overlap=true keeps the previous key published for the configured window; false removes every earlier key immediately. Needs Pro or Enterprise (or Vetted assurance); rate limited per configuration. Returns the current kid and published keys.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

overlap.description: true keeps the previous key for the overlap window; false drops all earlier keys immediately.

tools.name: list_signing_keys
tools.description: Lists a configuration's published key IDs, status, source and expiry. Available on every plan; returns no key material.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

tools.name: add_user
tools.description: Adds a fictional test user. user: { key, display_name?, sub?, icon?, access_token_sub?, claims?: { name: string|number|boolean|string[] }, claim_targets?: { name: both|id_token|access_token }, sign_in_outcome?: normal|access_denied|temporarily_unavailable|interaction_required|refresh_revoked (Pro) }.

configuration_id.description: The configuration id (from create_tenant or get_tenant).

key.description: The user key shown on the sign-in page and used as sub by default. Required when adding; fixed afterwards.

display_name.description: The name shown on the sign-in page and emitted as the name claim.

sub.description: The sub claim; the key when not set.

icon.description: A built-in icon id for the sign-in page.

access_token_sub.description: A different sub for access tokens only.

claims.description: The user's claims: name to a string, number, boolean or array of strings, e.g. { "email": "alice@example.com", "roles": ["admin"] }. Use fictional people only.

claim_targets.description: Which token each claim goes into: name to both (default), id_token or access_token.

sign_in_outcome.description: How sign-in goes for this user: normal (default), access_denied, temporarily_unavailable, interaction_required (prompt=none fails) or refresh_revoked (refreshing fails with invalid_grant). Any value other than normal is a Pro feature (plan_required otherwise).

user.description: The user, as in the Agent API. A fictional test user. On edit, fields left out keep their value; claims, when given, replaces the user's claims.
